Robot Doctor Code & OpModes

Can't deploy code from Android Studio

Control Hub not found, or the build won't install. Below are the 3 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 4 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Is the laptop connected to the robot's Wi-Fi network? Your laptop has to be on the Control Hub's network (or plugged in over USB-C).
  • Does the Control Hub show up in Android Studio's device list (or in "adb devices")? The device dropdown next to the Run button.
  • Did the build finish without errors and install on the Control Hub? Check the Build / Run panel at the bottom of Android Studio, or the OnBot Java build messages.
  • Is everything updated this season (Control Hub OS, hub firmware, Robot Controller and Driver Station apps)? The REV Hardware Client shows every version and whether an update is available.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Laptop isn't connected to the Control Hub

Wireless deploy needs your laptop on the robot's Wi-Fi and adb connected to it.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Join the laptop to the Control Hub's Wi-Fi network.
  2. In a terminal run adb connect 192.168.43.1:5555, then adb devices to confirm it shows up.
  3. If it shows "offline", run adb disconnect and connect again, or power cycle the hub.
  4. Leaving the REV Hardware Client open makes it connect adb to Control Hubs automatically.
  5. Over USB-C, use a cable that carries data, not a charge-only one.
Terminal
adb connect 192.168.43.1:5555
adb devices

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

2 Android Studio or SDK project is out of date

New Android Studio releases (Ladybug and later) changed things, and old SDK projects can fail to build or deploy.

How to fix it 30 min

  1. Update to the latest FtcRobotController SDK from GitHub and sync Gradle.
  2. Use an Android Studio version the current SDK supports (see the FtcRobotController README).
  3. Check the FTC Community forum for the current season's Android Studio threads. They come up every year.

Sources: FTC Docs · Recommended software versions

3 New code never made it to the robot

The build failed or was installed on a different device, so the robot is still running old code.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Read the bottom of the Android Studio Build / Run window for errors. A failed build installs nothing.
  2. Check the device dropdown in Android Studio shows your Control Hub before pressing Run.
  3. Add a version line to telemetry ("build 12") so you can always tell which code is on the robot.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues
